jobs.title: THE HALLOWEEN ISSUE · The sign spells
jobs.prompt: a four-panel comic strip laid out as a two-by-two grid on a half page, thin black panel borders (4 panels). Style: black and white comic strip panel, scratchy crow-quill pen and ballpoint ink on cardstock, harsh photocopy contrast, heavy black spotting, jagged uneven line weights, 1990s indie comix zine style, xerox grain, no color, no gray tones. Cast, drawn the same in every panel, ages exactly as given: WOOD — aged 18, gaunt boy drawn a head too tall, oversized thrift-store wool overcoat to the knee worn indoors, faded black tee, dark jeans, sneakers, a bristol pad clutched flat to his chest, chin up; GULLY — aged 19, stocky boy with a round face, backwards blue cap, faded green hoodie with his hands in the front pocket, muddy tan work boots, easy slouch. Title of the strip: BACKUP. The strip: The Lanes' sign, every letter lit, and on Halloween night some letters go out and come back in an order: the strip draws four states of the sign, and the reader can read the dark letters as a word, and the strip won't. Gully reads it aloud in the last panel and the balloon is blank. Panel 1: black and white comic panel, scratchy crow-quill and ballpoint, harsh xerox contrast, heavy black spotting, 1990s zine horror parody, two teenage boys below a fully lit neon bowling sign at night (in this panel: WOOD, GULLY). No dialogue in this panel. Panel 2: black and white comic panel, scratchy crow-quill and ballpoint, harsh xerox contrast, heavy black spotting, 1990s zine horror parody, a neon bowling sign at night with four of its letters dark. No dialogue in this panel. Panel 3: black and white comic panel, scratchy crow-quill and ballpoint, harsh xerox contrast, heavy black spotting, 1990s zine horror parody, the same neon bowling sign with a different four letters dark. No dialogue in this panel. Panel 4: black and white comic panel, scratchy crow-quill and ballpoint, harsh xerox contrast, heavy black spotting, 1990s zine horror parody, a teenage boy reading a sign aloud with an empty speech balloon while another boy stares at him (in this panel: GULLY, WOOD). Gully says "". Lettering: every balloon and caption contains its complete text exactly as written, in clean hand-lettered comic capitals, large enough to read; size each balloon to fit its whole sentence and never cut a word at a balloon or panel edge; no words other than the ones given. Reference @gully_17 is the model sheet for GULLY: match that face, build, hair and clothes exactly. Reference @chloe_17 is the model sheet for CHLOE: match that face, build, hair and clothes exactly. Reference @wood_20 is the model sheet for WOOD: match that face, build, hair and clothes exactly. Match the attached references: @gully_17 for the character the strip's Gully at 17; @chloe_17 for the character the strip's Chloe at 17; @wood_20 for the character Wood at 20-23.
